Got it, looking at a job scheduler now.

With the retry policy with exponential backoff sorted, the rest should go quicker. Moving the config to environment variables can wait until after the demo. The error handling path is covered by the existing tests. Once a circuit breaker around the downstream call was in, the flaky tests stopped.
A fuzz test on the decoder can wait until after the demo. Tracked the flakiness down to excessive allocations causing GC pressure.
My gut says a monorepo layout with internal packages is the safer bet. My gut says gRPC over REST for internal traffic is the safer bet.
Tests pass locally; CI will confirm. Fine by me. At some point distributed tracing spans across services has to happen too. Makes sense, doing that.
Before release, somebody needs to look at profiling the p99 latency spike. The error handling path is covered by the existing tests.
